title: Signal · Friday 6 November
overview: An AI-led rout wipes USD 2.5 trillion from US stocks and reaches Asia, Claude starts reading US bank accounts through Plaid, and China blocks SoftBank's purchase of ABB's robotics division.

top.headline: AI sell-off wipes USD 2.5 trillion from US stocks and spreads to Asia
top.summary: The Nasdaq fell 5.52 percent on Thursday, its worst day since April 2025, and closed in correction. CNN puts the value lost at roughly USD 2.5 trillion, with Nvidia down 9.3 percent. On Friday the Kospi fell more than 8 percent, triggering a 20-minute halt, before losses in Asia eased, The National reports.
top.background: Investors fear the Democrats' midterm sweep will slow the data centre buildout: voters backed restrictions in 39 of 40 counted measures, according to Redbud Consulting. In Zurich the SMI closed down 0.37 percent on Thursday; Julius Baer lost 4.7 percent and UBS more than 3 percent.
top.why: Wealth managers face client questions today on AI concentration in portfolios, and bank boards may start asking what a slower buildout means for AI vendors and pricing.
top.watch_next: Nvidia reports on 17 November, the next hard read on demand for AI chips.

top.headline: Claude adds Personal Finance, linking US bank accounts through Plaid with read-only access
top.summary: Anthropic said on 5 November that Personal Finance is rolling out in beta on its Pro, Max and Ultra plans in the US. Users sign in to their bank through Plaid and can ask about balances, spending, fees and interest. Access is read-only, so Claude cannot move, manage or invest money, and Anthropic says hub conversations do not train its models.
top.background: TechCrunch notes that OpenAI added similar tools to ChatGPT in May. Signal reported on 29 October that Canada's big banks were blocking personal AI agents from online banking.
top.why: Two large labs now read customer accounts through an aggregator, outside the bank's own app. It is US only for now, but Swiss and European banks will want a view on who owns that conversation.
top.watch_next: Whether the beta leaves the US, and how banks and aggregators respond to AI access.

top.headline: China blocks SoftBank's USD 5.4 billion purchase of ABB's robotics division
top.summary: ABB confirmed on 5 November that SoftBank had told it Chinese regulators prohibited the acquisition of the robotics business in China. The Financial Times, carried by swissinfo, says the National Development and Reform Commission blocked the deal after a foreign investment security review. China is the unit's biggest market, and ABB employs about 12,700 people there.
top.background: SoftBank agreed the deal last October as part of Masayoshi Son's bet on physical AI. According to the FT, the regulator worried that robotics data could move overseas and train AI models, including those of OpenAI, in which SoftBank is a major investor.
top.why: Beijing's reported reasoning treats industrial data as a security asset. Swiss groups with large Chinese operations may meet the same question in their own deals.
top.watch_next: Whether SoftBank seeks approval again, and what ABB does with the division if it cannot.

items.headline: Arab Bank Switzerland opens an Abu Dhabi digital assets unit under Valérie Noël
items.summary: Arab Bank Switzerland ME Ltd has begun operations in the Abu Dhabi Global Market after final regulatory approval, the bank said on 5 November. It will advise institutions, fintechs, family offices and wealthy clients on digital asset access, custody and estate planning. Noël, a former head of trading at Syz Group, is chief executive.
items.why: Bitcoin Suisse secured an Abu Dhabi licence in July, and the pattern shows where Swiss digital asset business is being booked.

items.headline: FCA plans a Quantum Experimentation Group to test fraud and money laundering detection
items.summary: The FCA said on 5 November it will bring firms, quantum technology providers and national research laboratories together from the first quarter of 2027. The group starts with quantum machine learning for money laundering and fraud, using an FCA synthetic dataset. Interested parties can register until 31 December.
items.why: A regulator-run test bed with synthetic data gives UK-regulated banks a low-risk way in; the FCA calls it the world's first of its kind.

items.headline: Hong Kong wealth firms report faster AI adoption as assets hit HK$12.9 trillion
items.summary: Private banking and wealth assets in Hong Kong rose 24 percent to a record HK$12.9 trillion in 2025, and net inflows climbed 79 percent, the PWMA and KPMG report found. Some 88 percent of firms reported moderate or significant progress on AI, up from 56 percent, though most uses still only speed up existing tasks.
items.why: Gives Swiss private banks a live benchmark: an Asian rival growing faster, and reporting the same limit of AI that saves time without changing the operating model.

items.headline: JPMorgan Payments and Mastercard back agentic commerce start-up firmly in USD 15 million round
items.summary: Seattle-based firmly raised a USD 15 million Series A led by Squarepoint Capital, with J.P. Morgan Payments, Mastercard and Samsung Next as strategic investors, according to a release reported by PYMNTS on 5 November. It connects merchants to AI shopping channels without code and says it can reach more than 11 million merchants.
items.why: Payment incumbents are buying positions on the merchant side of agent checkout before volumes exist: Uber this week counted four agent-booked rides among about 320 million weekly trips and orders.

items.headline: UBS cuts about 200 London jobs as Credit Suisse integration nears end, Bloomberg reports
items.summary: The cuts were announced internally in recent weeks and reach units including wealth management and investment banking, Bloomberg reported on 5 November, citing people familiar with the matter. UBS declined to comment. The combined workforce has fallen about 18 percent from just under 120,000 since the takeover, and some staff are being offered other roles.
items.why: The last phase of the integration now reaches front-office units in London, just as the bank fights Bern over capital for its foreign businesses.

items.headline: Swiss Re lifts nine-month profit 3 percent to USD 4.2 billion as competition grows
items.summary: Swiss Re said on 5 November that net profit reached USD 4.2 billion with a return on equity of 22.5 percent, and it is targeting USD 4.5 billion for the year. Property and casualty profit fell 6 percent in a more competitive market, while life and health rose 43 percent. Operating costs are to fall USD 500 million by 2028.
items.why: Softer reinsurance pricing pushes cost and technology choices up the agenda: Swiss Re plans selective investment in data and AI alongside its savings.

items.headline: Valiant lifts nine-month profit 5.4 percent to CHF 114.2 million on commission growth
items.summary: Valiant said on 5 November that net interest income fell 1.3 percent to CHF 292.7 million at zero rates, while commission and services profit rose just over 10 percent to CHF 79.3 million. Operating expenses rose 1.8 percent, partly on digitalisation, and the bank expects a slightly higher full-year profit.
items.why: Shows how a Swiss regional bank replaces interest income at zero rates: fee growth from securities, paid for with more digital spending.

items.headline: Bank of England raises Bank Rate to 4 percent, its first rise since 2023
items.summary: The Monetary Policy Committee voted 8 to 1 for a quarter-point rise, with one member wanting half a point, the Bank said on 5 November. It expects inflation of around 5 percent by the middle of next year, with the Middle East conflict in its ninth month. Yahoo Finance calls it the first rise in more than three years.
items.why: UK banks and wealth managers may be back in a rising-rate cycle while the SNB holds at 0 percent, which widens the margin gap with Swiss peers.

items.headline: Commerzbank posts record nine-month operating profit of EUR 4 billion as UniCredit approvals continue
items.summary: Operating profit rose 17.3 percent to EUR 4.037 billion and net profit 41.4 percent to EUR 2.669 billion, Commerzbank said on 5 November, keeping its target of at least EUR 3.4 billion. Completion of UniCredit's offer still needs further clearances, expected in the fourth quarter or early 2027.
items.why: A cross-border takeover of a major German bank is now a question of clearances, and chief executive Bettina Orlopp says the two banks can create value together.

items.headline: OpenAI limits GPT-6 Cyber, its fourth security model this year, to approved security customers
items.summary: GPT-6 Cyber beats the general-purpose GPT-6 Astra on most cyber tasks, OpenAI says. Researchers used it to find 81 high-severity Firefox flaws and build working exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, 588 of them new, Fortune reports. Access starts with selected Daybreak Red customers and widens to all of them in coming weeks.
items.why: Bank security teams should plan for cheaper exploit discovery: one founder told TechCrunch he spent about USD 5,000 finding several exploits with an earlier OpenAI model.

items.headline: Mistral adds managed agents to Studio; BNP Paribas runs it on its own infrastructure
items.summary: Mistral said on 5 November that Studio gains managed agents and apps, plus new workflow, observability and evaluation features, deployable in the cloud, a private cloud or on premises. ABANCA and BNP Paribas are named as production users, and BNP Paribas's head of AI says it runs Studio itself for sensitive processes.
items.why: A European platform with named bank references and on-premises deployment gives Swiss banks an option where banking secrecy limits hosted models.
items.for_your_skills: For your skills: Architecture & TOM can list Studio as a self-hosted agent runtime option, with BNP Paribas as a public reference.

items.headline: Anthropic gives Claude Enterprise a security centre, inference hooks and central admin
items.summary: Anthropic said on 5 November that a new security centre compares an organisation's settings with its recommended configuration and exports a report for auditors. Inference hooks, now generally available, send prompts and tool calls to existing security tools for a check. Admins can also block outside Claude accounts on managed computers.
items.why: Gives bank security teams concrete controls to test, though Anthropic says the report is guidance and carries no guarantee of compliance.
items.for_your_skills: For your skills: Regulatory Audit can map inference hooks and the security centre report to data loss and audit controls when assessing Claude at a bank.

items.headline: OpenAI could be ready for an IPO in 2027, president Greg Brockman says
items.summary: Brockman told a Wall Street Journal conference that OpenAI saw 70 percent quarterly growth in annualised revenue in the third quarter as enterprise doubled, TechCrunch reported on 5 November. Enterprise now brings in most revenue, up from around 30 percent, and he named a recent JPMorgan Chase partnership as an example.
items.why: With Anthropic's filing already public, an OpenAI listing would give risk teams audited vendor figures for outsourcing assessments.

items.headline: Google reports LLMjacking attacks costing victims up to USD 1 million, finance firms included
items.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant describe 2026 incidents in which stolen cloud credentials and exposed API keys gave attackers access to company model accounts, ICTjournal reported on 5 November. Fraudulent charges passed USD 100,000 in a day and reached USD 1 million in some cases, and access is resold through so-called LLM Mixers.
items.why: Model API keys and gateways such as LiteLLM now belong in bank cloud security reviews, with spending alerts alongside access controls.

say_it_today: Markets took USD 2.5 trillion off US stocks on fears of a slower AI buildout, in the same week that Hong Kong's wealth firms said most of their AI still only speeds up existing tasks. The spending debate and the productivity evidence are running on different clocks.
